claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain residual interfacial stress.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
The residual stresses and compositional heterogeneities arise from the non-equiatomic deposition process.
Residual interfacial stress and nanoscale compositional heterogeneity produce localized variations in magnetic anisotropy.
Localized magnetic-anisotropy variations govern the reduced magnetocaloric response of the as-deposited films or nanoribbons.
Localized magnetic-anisotropy variations govern enhanced hysteresis under low-applied-field cycling.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will relieve residual interfacial stress.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will reduce nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Reducing residual stress and compositional heterogeneity will produce a more uniform magnetic-domain structure.
A more uniform magnetic-domain structure will make magnetization changes during field cycling more reversible.
More reversible magnetization changes will enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
More reversible magnetization changes will reduce hysteretic energy dissipation.
Annealed films or nanoribbons will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change per cycle than the as-deposited control.
Annealed films or nanoribbons will exhibit lower hysteretic losses than the as-deposited control.
Intrinsic heat-transfer rate limits the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Interfacial and edge effects dominate in nanoscale thin films and patterned nanoribbons under the stated conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to bulk samples or films that undergo extensive grain growth.
